'''Thorvald Nicolai Thiele''' (24 December 1838 – 26 September 1910) was a [[Denmark|Danish]] [[astronomer]] and director of the [[Copenhagen Observatory]].<ref name="springer" /> He was also an [[actuary]] and [[mathematician]], most notable for his work in [[statistics]], [[interpolation]] and the [[N-body problem#Three-body problem|three-body problem]].

Thiele made notable contributions to the statistical study of random time series and introduced the [[cumulant]]s and [[likelihood function]]s, and was considered to be one of the greatest statisticians of all time by [[Ronald Fisher]].<ref>Jerzy Neyman, “Note on an Article by Sir Ronald Fisher,” ''Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B (Methodological)'', 18, 2 (July 1956): 288–294, {{doi|10.1111/j.2517-6161.1956.tb00236.x}}.</ref> In the early 1900s he also developed and proposed a generalisation of [[approval voting]] to multiple winner elections called [[sequential proportional approval voting]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=((Reuterskiöld)) |first1=C. A. |last2=Phragmén |first2=E. |last3=Svensén |first3=Emil |last4=Huss |first4=E. G. |last5=Fahlbeck |first5=Pontus E. |last6=Alin |first6=Oscar |year=1899 |title=1899 Vol. 2 no. 2 |url=http://journals.lub.lu.se/index.php/st/article/view/1949/1528&usg=ALkJrhiuUQ1zCqZHnca_-iAmk1KpNqMtmg |journal=Statsvetenskaplig Tidskrift |volume=2 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150618072022/http://journals.lub.lu.se/index.php/st/article/view/1949/1528%26usg%3DALkJrhiuUQ1zCqZHnca_-iAmk1KpNqMtmg |archive-date=2015-06-18}}</ref> which was briefly used for party lists in [[Sweden]] when proportional representation was introduced in 1909.

Thiele also was a founder and Mathematical Director of the [[Codan A/S|Hafnia Insurance Company]] and led the founding of the [[Danish Society of Actuaries]]. It was through his [[insurance]] work that he came into contact with fellow mathematician [[Jørgen Pedersen Gram]].

Thiele was the father of astronomer [[Holger Thiele]].

The main-belt asteroids [[843 Nicolaia]] (discovered by his son Holger) and [[1586 Thiele]] are named in his honour.<ref name="springer" />
